blocks.text: EXCLUSIVE: Gregg Araki has wrapped production on his dark comedy The Decline of F*cking Western Civilization , with 12 additions rounding out a stacked cast, sources tell Deadline.

links.text: The Decline of F*cking Western Civilization

blocks.text: They are: Kal Penn ( Trust Me, I’m a Doctor ), Michael Chiklis ( The Senior ), David Koechner ( Anchorman ), Nat Faxon ( Loot ), Wendi McLendon-Covey ( The Goldbergs ), Steve Guttenberg ( Three Men and a Baby ), actor-producer Colleen Camp ( Euphoria ), Giovanni Ribisi ( American Hostage ), Judy Greer ( In Memoriam ), Margaret Cho ( I Want Your Sex ), Lulu Wilson ( Becky ), and Charlie Bushnell ( Percy Jackson and the Olympians ).

blocks.text: Gregg Araki Sets Ashton Kutcher & Alison Brie For Dark Comedy 'The Decline of F*cking Western Civilization'; Jesse Williams In Talks

links.text: Gregg Araki Sets Ashton Kutcher & Alison Brie For Dark Comedy 'The Decline of F*cking Western Civilization'; Jesse Williams In Talks

blocks.text: This troupe supports the previously announced Ashton Kutcher, Alison Brie, and Jesse Williams. No character details have emerged.
Little is known about the film, other than it being an ensemble piece comped as Election meets American Beauty . Production kicked off in Los Angeles in mid September.

Producers are Why Not Productions and Goodfellas. Araki is working from a script by Kevin W. Koehler, on which he’s completed revisions. The lauded indie filmmaker comes to the project on the heels of I Want You Sex , a darkly comedic erotic thriller starring Olivia Wilde and Cooper Hoffman, which released with Magnolia Pictures this summer after premiering to critical acclaim at Sundance.

Penn is repped by UTA, Anonymous Content, and Fuller Law; Chiklis by UTA, Entertainment 360, and Ziffren Brittenham; Koechner by Gersh and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller; Faxon by CAA, Artists First, Untitled, and Goodman, Genow, Schenkman; McLendon-Covey by UTA, John Carrabino Management, and Yorn, Levine, Barnes; Guttenberg by CAA and Vault Entertainment; Camp by Gersh; Ribisi by CAA, Linden Entertainment, and Hansen, Jacobson, Teller; Greer by CAA, Artists First, and Toczek Suddleson; Cho by WME, manager Sarah J. Martin, and Fox Rothschild; Wilson by UTA, Authentic, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman; and Bushnell by Vault Entertainment and Myman Greenspan Fox.
